NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Operator standard instructions for joining Q&A queue.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Johnathan Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Emily Carter, Head of Commercial; Tom Whitaker, Head of Manufacturing; and Dr. Karen Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by blockbuster growth in our oncology and immunology franchises, robust volume expansion, and strategic gains in emerging markets. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including advancing our precision biologics pipeline, optimizing manufacturing efficiencies, and executing on commercial launches amid a competitive landscape with biosimilar pressures and payer dynamics.

Today, I'll provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. Our marketing and sales teams achieved category-leading effectiveness, with return on investment metrics outperforming peers through targeted campaigns and AI-driven personalization. Geographically, we saw balanced growth, with emerging markets accelerating at triple-digit rates thanks to regulatory wins and localized partnerships. On product performance, key franchises like oncology and immunology drove double-digit revenue increases via strong volume uptake and stable pricing. Gross margins expanded meaningfully due to process optimizations and scale-up investments. We're updating revenue guidance upward, supported by stacked pipeline catalysts such as Phase 3 readouts and PDUFA dates. Overall, we're highlighting record quarterly results, margin leverage, and derisked clinical momentum. Key assumptions underpin our outlook, balanced against risks like regulatory delays and competition, while new launches are capturing meaningful market share rapidly.

We are particularly excited about NovaLumab, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody, and its potential to dominate in NSCLC and beyond, with share gains closing in on category leaders.

Now, I will turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Johnathan Hale, CFO:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in our oncology portfolio, new product contributions from immunology assets like ImmunoGuard, and outsized expansion in emerging markets, partially offset by some biosimilar erosion on legacy products.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $650 million, or $2.15 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $850 million, or $2.80 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.4 billion, reflecting disciplined investments in R&D at 30% of revenue to fuel our pipeline, alongside SG&A efficiencies that reduced that line as a percentage of sales to 22%. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our biologics and gene therapy pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $4.2 billion.

Diving deeper into our overall performance highlights, we posted record Q3 revenue of $2.8 billion, surpassing our guidance midpoint by $150 million. Oncology led with $1.46 billion, up 32% year-over-year, powered by ONC-427's $850 million following label expansions in breast cancer. Rare diseases and gene therapies added $750 million, up 25%, with GENEVO at $420 million on strong European reimbursement. Immunology contributed $450 million, up 22%, as ILUMIRA gained share in psoriasis. Ex-U.S. revenues hit 38% of total, growing 35%. Adjusted non-GAAP EPS was $2.15, up 35%, with gross margins at 84.2% from manufacturing gains and favorable mix. Free cash flow reached $1.1 billion, supporting $500 million in share repurchases.

On product revenue by key franchises, oncology delivered $1.42 billion, up 22%, with ONC-301 volumes up 14% to 285,000 units on 28% NRx growth in NSCLC to 42% U.S. share; ASP rose 7% to $42,500. Immunology hit $850 million, up 15%, volumes up 11% to 1.2 million patient-months, ASP up 4% to $18,200. Rare diseases reached $380 million, up 28%, with 1,800 doses and stable $2.1 million U.S. ASP. Volume drove 65% of growth, pricing 25%.

Geographically, North America was 54% or $691 million, up 18% on NovaLumab demand. Europe 26% or $333 million, up 15% CER on reimbursement. ROW 20% or $256 million, up 42%, with emerging markets at $154 million, surging 58%. Asia ex-Japan $112 million, China $78 million post-NRDL. Latin America $28 million, up 65%. This stems from 14 NDA filings at 85% approval, $250 million in regional hubs, and tiered pricing.

Gross margins hit 82.5%, up 340 bps YoY, with TTM at 81.8%; FY guide 83-85%. Mix added 200 bps from 65% high-margin oncology; efficiencies 140 bps, COGS down 15% to $28/gram via 22% titer gains to 9.8 g/L, continuous manufacturing at 75% utilization, and regional footprints like Singapore at 90% for biosimilars.

For marketing and sales effectiveness, underpinning 18% net sales growth to $2.8 billion amid payer scrutiny and biosimilar erosion like 25% adalimumab share loss, ROMI reached 4.2x from 3.8x. ImmunoGuard $1.2 billion, up 22%, TRx 4.5 million up 15%, NRx up 28%; reps averaged 8.2 calls/day, 14% conversion lift. Oncology OncoTarget $850 million, up 35%, 18% NSCLC share, SOV 28%, CAC $450 down 17%. US 65% $1.8 billion, DTC 6.1x ROMI. Europe €520 million, 3.5x ROMI. APAC $280 million up 45%. AI "Next Best Action" boosted productivity 20%, SG&A down to 22%.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $11.5 billion to $12.0 billion in revenue, 26-33% growth at midpoint, and non-GAAP EPS $9.00 to $9.50. Q4 $720-760 million. Key upcoming catalysts: Q1 2025 Phase 3 NOV-101-302 PFS data HR 0.62 in breast cancer for BLA mid-2025; March 15 PDUFA for NOV-303 Pompe expansion; Lilly co-dev term sheet; continuous manufacturing COGS down 18%. FY2025 $3.4-3.6 billion.

Key assumptions: mid-single volume growth, 12-15% ex-US, 65-70% PTS for NovaLink-301, R&D 22-24%, margins +150 bps. Risks: Phase 3 misses, biosimilars eroding 15-20% share, pricing declines 4-6%, supply disruptions, IP challenges, macro pressures.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Chen, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Johnathan. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, topline Phase 3 VISTA-3 data for ONC-427 in ovarian cancer showed HR 0.68; GENEVO 95% event-free survival at 3 years; CART-19x dosing initiated. Over 5,000 patients dosed in 12 Phase III trials, 70% readouts H2 2024. We expect to report additional data from NovaLink-301 interim and file for expansions in Q4.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Advancements include AI proteomics with Tempus accelerating hit ID by 40%; preclinical OBEX-101 GLP-1 agonist with best-in-class PK; CRISPR alliances for gene editing; SynthoRx acquisition adding Phase II NASH/ALS assets. We're advancing bispecific T-cell engagers and ADCs, with IND clearances in China.

Now I'll turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Emily Carter, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with new product launches driving $500 million+ in revenue. VirexLir-7 GLP-1 hit $285 million Q3, 12% new script share vs. Ozempic/Mounjaro, 185,000 NBRx on 22% A1c drop; VirexBispec-23 $112 million, 14% LBCL share. VirexTarg-9 up 15% to $420 million, 22% HER2 share. U.S. launches with 65% formulary, ex-U.S. building via EMA/PMDA. Marketing campaigns proved effective, with omnichannel ROMI 4.2x, digital video 5.2x, patient programs boosting adherence to 92%.

Next, Tom Whitaker will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Whitaker, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Emily. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity at Devens and Singapore at 120% utilization for bispecifics, yields up 22% to 9.8 g/L, continuous platforms reducing COGS 15-18% and lead times to 4 months. Supply chain resilient with $250-450 million investments, regional JVs, single-use tech cutting downtime 40%. Key priorities: scale for gene therapies, net-zero emissions by 2026, tech transfers for new launches.

Finally, Dr. Karen Lee will provide an update on regulatory submissions and approvals.

Dr. Karen Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thank you, Tom. We continue to work closely with regulatory agencies. Recent wins: EMA for NovaLumab frontline, FDA RMAT for NOV-303, PMDA fast-track for Japan launches, 85% approval on 14 BRICS+ NDAs. Ongoing: BLA for ONC-427 Q4 PDUFA, sNDA for expansions, CHMP for bispecifics. Interactions focus on bridging studies, HTA dossiers, and post-approval commitments amid IRA/HTA reforms.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Thank you, Karen. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from David Lerner with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lerner, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On emerging markets growth to 12% of revenue, can you elaborate on the sustainability given FX and IP risks?

Johnathan Hale, CFO:
Thanks, David. Emerging markets' 58% surge to $154 million reflects regulatory playbook with 85% NDA success via U.S./EU bridging, supply hubs cutting COGS 15%, tiered pricing like $42k U.S. vs. $14k China. FX shaved 2 points, but we forecast 18% of revenue by FY2026 at 25% CAGR, de-risked by co-pay/digital platforms. IP mitigated via local JVs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. Regarding gross margin expansion to 82.5%, what are the biggest drivers for FY24 guide of 83-85%?

Tom Whitaker, Head of Manufacturing:
Maria, thanks. 340 bps YoY from 200 bps mix (65% oncology), 140 bps efficiencies: titers to 9.8 g/L, continuous at 75% utilization, AI maintenance cuts. NC expansion adds 80,000L; risks like resin inflation baked in at 50 bps conservative.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim, Morgan Stanley:
On new launches like VirexLir-7 at 12% share, how do you see competition evolving, and Q4 ramp?

Emily Carter, Head of Commercial:
Alex, VirexLir-7's edge in tolerability and injector drove 220% QoQ to $285 million; $1.2B FY25 peak via monthly/oral filings. Competitors' shortages funnel switchers; we guide 25% new product CAGR with capacity ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Patel with Citi. Please go ahead.

Sarah Patel, Citi:
Thanks. For catalysts like NOV-101-302 Q1 data, what's the HR confidence and revenue impact?

Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer:
Sarah, HR 0.62 in HER2-low breast met PFS primary; $5B TAM unlock, $800M 2026 incremental. 65-70% PTS based on interim/ADC benchmarks; BLA mid-2025 on track.

Operator:
Thank you. One more from the line of Peter Wong with Barclays.

Peter Wong, Barclays:
Quick one on ROMI 4.2x and AI tools—any quantification on EPS accretion?

Johnathan Hale, CFO:
Peter, ROMI up from 3.8x via Veeva AI personalizing 75% interactions, 20% rep productivity, SG&A to 22%; 25% EPS accretion from efficiencies, supporting $8.50 LT target.

Dr. Michael Reynolds, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
